hook: Your circadian rhythm is not a preference. It is a 24-hour biological clock running on light signals — and most people are giving it completely the wrong inputs.
topic: Circadian biology, light as the primary zeitgeber, morning and evening timing
body:
**The circadian system is regulated by a cluster of neurons in the hypothalamus called the suprachiasmatic nucleus. It runs on a roughly 24-hour cycle and uses one primary input to calibrate itself: light.**

Specifically — short-wavelength blue light hitting the retina triggers a signal to the SCN that anchors your internal clock to external time. The timing of that signal is everything. Morning light exposure suppresses melatonin, elevates cortisol appropriately, and sets your clock forward. Evening light — from screens, overhead lighting, devices — sends the same wake signal at the wrong time, delaying the melatonin onset your brain needs to prepare for sleep.

Most people do this in reverse. They wake up and stay indoors. They spend the evening bathed in artificial light. The result is a circadian clock that is perpetually confused about what time it is.

The single highest-leverage intervention for sleep quality is not a supplement, not a gadget, not a wind-down routine. It is ten minutes of outdoor light within thirty minutes of waking, and a reduction in bright light in the two hours before bed.

The mechanism responds to those inputs immediately and consistently. Every single morning.

More detail in the guide — link in bio.
